goal: Implement an in-repo CUDA kernel aligned with flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe for real TP=1 G11 packed NVFP4 MoE, and beat FlashInfer performance.

current_source_state.status: best committed source kept; negative experiments reverted

recent_rejected_experiments.summary: Warp-per-token routing regressed end-to-end latency to about 3275.94us; source reverted.
Atomic metadata and fused metadata+hidden pack were not accepted because end-to-end correctness was intermittent or total latency regressed; source kept at best state.
GEMM2 warp-shuffle variants showed up to about 70us potential but produced intermittent full-output corruption; do not switch default without full-output localization and repeated correctness reruns.
Padding-only zero for SwiGLU/requant was correct but regressed end-to-end latency to about 2841.02us; source reverted.

untracked_files_policy.status: Historical profile/log files and the separate kernel_opt_fused_moe_pes directory are left untracked.
untracked_files_policy.reason: They are either temporary outputs, older experiment artifacts, or unrelated nested worktree content. The recoverable state is captured by committed memory records and selected tracked profiles.

recommended_next_steps: If pursuing the GEMM2 warp-shuffle speedup, compare full gemm2_out from stable postsync versus the warp-shuffle variant and localize corrupted rows, columns, expert ids, and CTA ranks before retesting.
For larger gains, investigate fusing GEMM2 epilogue with top-k weighted scatter or otherwise eliminating the GEMM2 output/final-scatter memory round trip.
Keep FlashInfer as the baseline/oracle and continue using real G11 packed NVFP4 activation plus FlashInfer prepared weight layout.
